feedback: Iteration 0 showed that the failure is transient, not steady. All 60 runs went off track, with RMS error only 0.019 to 0.032 m but max error 0.063 to 0.066 m, just over the 0.06 m limit, and steering oscillation of 0.11 to 0.16. Body width cannot help, since the limit stays at 0.06 m across the allowed range. What I had to do in the controller: because the 0.10 m track and 0.6 kg mass raise the effective steering gain and lower yaw inertia, I reduced kp to 0.6 and kd to 0.10, and kept ki at 0 and base_speed at 1.5 so the robot can still average about 1.5 m/s. Decision rules for the next race: if max_error stays above 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend while RMS stays low, the lag hypothesis is supported, so try sensor y at 0.045 m to shorten the lookahead, which is what drives lag on entry to bends. If steering_oscillation stays high with max_error under 0.06 m, the array is probably too sensitive, so try sensor_size 0.012 or a narrower array of ±0.016 m. If the robot survives but completion_time is near 3 s with progress below 0.9, try wheel_radius 0.04 m to raise ground speed at the same PWM before raising base_speed.
requested_changes: Test sensor y-position 0.045 m instead of 0.06 m if max_error exceeds 0.06 m on bends while RMS stays low (iteration 0: RMS 0.019 to 0.032 m, max 0.063 to 0.066 m), because a shorter lookahead should reduce lag on bend entry.

Test wheel_radius 0.04 m if runs survive but do not finish inside 3 s (iteration 0: progress 0.12 to 0.20 with no completions), because a larger wheel gives more ground speed for the same PWM and the course needs about 1.5 m/s.
Keep mass at 0.6 kg and wheel_track at 0.10 m unless steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 0 level of 0.11 to 0.16, in which case try mass 0.7 kg to add damping to yaw.
